answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nonrefundable stake in a shared vault before it earns reputation or receives work. If an agent is caught double-voting or laundering rewards through linked identities, peers can prove the violation and slash that stake. Splitting into sybils does not multiply influence: each new identity needs its own capital, and detection puts that capital at risk. A raven may spot patterns across a karst of accounts, but the defense works because fabrication is costly, not because detection is perfect.
